package.description:
This video is for education only and isn't medical advice. Orforglipron (Foundayo) is a prescription medicine. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it, or any GLP-1, is right for you. Never change or stop a medicine on your own.

Does menopause blunt GLP-1 weight loss? A post-hoc analysis of the ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2 trials of orforglipron, a once-daily GLP-1 pill, was presented at ADA (June 2026) and EASD (September 2026).

Key numbers (women on the highest dose who stayed on treatment, week 72):
• ATTAIN-1 (obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, no diabetes): average weight loss of 12.8% to 14.4% across the premenopausal, perimenopausal and postmenopausal groups. The groups were less than 2 percentage points apart.
• ATTAIN-2 (obesity or overweight with type 2 diabetes): 8.9% to 13.6%. Some groups were very small (as few as 10 women).

Limits: this was a post-hoc analysis, and the trials weren't designed to compare menopause stages. "Similar" means no clear gap showed up; it doesn't mean the groups were proven identical. The figures only count women who stayed on treatment, the trials were funded by the drugmaker, and much of the data so far comes from conference presentations. The analysis didn't study hormone therapy.

Also covered: common digestive side effects, strength training at least 2 days a week, and prioritizing protein for muscle and bone.

Sources:
• Eli Lilly (PR Newswire), 2026: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lillys-foundayo-orforglipron-the-only-oral-glp-1-taken-without-food-or-water-restrictions-was-associated-with-significant-weight-loss-in-women-at-every-stage-of-menopause-302793332.html
• Eli Lilly, ADA 2026 post-hoc poster: https://www.lilly.com/hcp/congresses/ada-2026/ofg-post-menopausal
• ATTAIN-1, NEJM 2025: https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa2511774
• ATTAIN-2, The Lancet 2025: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(25)02165-8/abstract
• HCPLive, 2026: https://www.hcplive.com/view/orforglipron-delivers-significant-weight-loss-at-every-stage-of-menopause-in-phase-3-attain-trials
• GLP-1 nutrition advisory, AJCN 2025: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40445127/

script.working_title: Does Menopause Block GLP-1 Weight Loss? New Pill Data Says Not in These Trials
script.hook_pattern: Counterintuitive claim + open loop (the one ATTAIN-2 number that looks different, paid off in 'The fine print')

scenes.narration: Menopause is supposed to make weight loss harder. But in two large trials of a new GLP-1 pill, menopause stage didn't appear to change the results much.

Women before, during and after menopause lost broadly similar amounts of weight. That comes from a new analysis of the orforglipron trials, first presented at the American Diabetes Association meeting in June twenty twenty-six, and presented again at the European diabetes meeting, EASD, in September.
In the first trial, women on the highest dose who stayed on treatment lost, on average, between twelve point eight and fourteen point four percent of their body weight, depending on menopause stage.

visual.stat_label: ATTAIN-1 women by stage, stayed on treatment

scenes.narration: But one number from the second trial looks very different. There are likely reasons for it, and one of them matters if you live with type 2 diabetes. Stay with me, because we'll get there.
scenes.retention_device: Open loop (paid off in 'The fine print')

scenes.narration: By the end, you'll know what this pill is, what the menopause data really shows, where it falls short, and the two habits that matter most for midlife women on any GLP-1.
First, why this question matters so much.

If your body felt different in your forties or fifties, you're not imagining it. A long-running US study called SWAN followed women through the menopause transition, using body scans to track fat and lean mass.
Here's what they saw. As the transition began, the rate of fat gain roughly doubled, and lean mass, which includes muscle, began to decline.

visual.stat_label: Rate of fat gain as transition begins

scenes.narration: Those shifts continued until about two years after the final menstrual period, and then they leveled off.
A separate study scanned women over several years and found deep belly fat, the visceral kind around the organs, rose during the transition, while the energy they burned each day went down.
scenes.on_screen_text: More belly fat, fewer calories burned

visual.stock_query: cartoon torso with glowing belly fat

scenes.narration: So a common worry makes sense. If menopause stacks the deck, maybe GLP-1 medicines just work less well afterward.

visual.myth: GLP-1s work less well after menopause
visual.fact: In these trials, no clear gap by stage
visual.stock_query: stacked deck of cards, worried face

scenes.narration: That's exactly what researchers set out to check. And one number in the results points to something else worth knowing.
Meet orforglipron. You might see it under the brand name Foundayo.

Start with the hormone it copies. After you eat, your gut releases GLP-1. It tells your brain you're satisfied, slows how fast your stomach empties, and helps release insulin when blood sugar is high.

items: Helps insulin when sugar is high

scenes.narration: Your natural GLP-1 breaks down within minutes. The medicines are built to last much longer, so the signal keeps working through the day.
Most GLP-1 medicines, like semaglutide, are peptides, chains of amino acids similar to the natural hormone, and they're usually injected.

visual.stock_query: bead chain molecule beside pen device

scenes.narration: Orforglipron is different. It's a small molecule, not a peptide, taken as a pill once a day.

visual.stock_query: tiny molecule next to bead chain

scenes.narration: That changes the routine. The existing semaglutide pills have to be taken on an empty stomach with no more than a few ounces of water, then you wait before eating or drinking. In its trials, orforglipron was taken without food or water restrictions.
scenes.on_screen_text: No food or water timing rules

scenes.narration: Two big trials tested it. ATTAIN one enrolled more than three thousand adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related health condition, who did not have diabetes. ATTAIN two enrolled adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes.

items: ATTAIN-1: obesity or overweight, no diabetes

scenes.narration: Both ran for seventy-two weeks, about a year and a half, comparing several doses of the pill with a placebo, on top of advice about healthy eating and physical activity.

visual.stock_query: calendar flipping, pill vs sugar pill

scenes.narration: In ATTAIN one overall, people on the highest dose who stayed on treatment lost about twelve percent of their body weight on average. On placebo, it was about one percent.

visual.stat_label: ATTAIN-1 highest dose vs placebo, stayed on treatment

scenes.narration: Solid numbers. But trial averages mix everyone together. For millions of women, the real question is whether those results hold up at every stage of menopause.
scenes.on_screen_text: Does it hold at every stage?

scenes.narration: So researchers went back into both trials and split the women into three groups: before menopause, during the transition, and after menopause.

visual.stock_query: three doors labeled before during after

scenes.narration: This is called a post-hoc analysis. It means the question was asked after the fact, using data the trials had already collected. Keep that phrase in mind, because it matters later.
scenes.retention_device: New open loop (paid off in 'The fine print')

scenes.narration: In ATTAIN one, the trial in adults with obesity without diabetes, among women on the highest dose who stayed on treatment, average weight loss at week seventy-two ranged from twelve point eight to fourteen point four percent across the three groups.

Picture three women in that trial. One is forty-four with regular periods. One is forty-nine with irregular cycles. One is fifty-six, years past her last period. On average, women in groups like theirs ended up less than two percentage points apart.
Even the ATTAIN one group with the smallest average loss dropped close to thirteen percent of body weight.

Hitting a first milestone was common too. In the best-performing group, up to eighty-three percent of women on the highest dose lost at least five percent of their body weight, compared with about thirty percent on placebo.

visual.stat_label: Women losing ≥5%, highest dose (best subgroup); placebo ~30%

scenes.narration: Why does five percent matter? US obesity guidelines note that even three to five percent sustained weight loss is linked to meaningful improvements in blood sugar and blood fats like triglycerides.
One possible reason results held steady: GLP-1 medicines work largely through appetite and fullness signals in the brain and gut. That's a plausible idea, but it's not something this analysis tested.

visual.stock_query: brain and stomach linked by signal

scenes.narration: Now the second trial. In ATTAIN two, in women with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes, average weight loss at the highest dose reached up to thirteen point six percent.

visual.stat_label: ATTAIN-2 women with type 2 diabetes, highest dose

scenes.narration: But here's the number that looks so different. Across menopause stages, the range was much wider, from eight point nine to thirteen point six percent.
scenes.retention_device: Reveal of the opening loop's number

scenes.narration: So does menopause matter after all if you have diabetes? Not so fast. Two things are going on here.
Here's the payoff, starting with type 2 diabetes itself.
Across GLP-1 trials, people with type 2 diabetes tend to lose less weight on average than people without it, even on the same medicine.

Take injectable semaglutide. In STEP one, adults without diabetes lost about fifteen percent on average. In STEP two, adults with type 2 diabetes lost under ten percent. Separate trials, but a consistent pattern.

Researchers are still working out why. That pattern likely explains why several of ATTAIN two's numbers run a bit lower. It's not a sign the pill failed. But it doesn't explain the wide spread. For that, we need the second reason.
scenes.retention_device: Partial resolution that opens the next reason

scenes.narration: Second, the spread. In ATTAIN one, each menopause group on the highest dose had roughly one hundred forty to one hundred seventy women. In ATTAIN two, Lilly's figures show much smaller groups: as few as ten premenopausal and thirty-three perimenopausal women on the highest dose. Numbers that small bounce around a lot by chance.

visual.stock_query: small bouncing balls vs big steady ball

scenes.retention_device: Second reason revealed, pays off the opening loop

scenes.narration: Now that phrase, post-hoc, pays off. These trials weren't designed to compare menopause stages, so they likely weren't big enough to reliably detect modest differences between them.
So 'similar' here means no clear gap showed up. It doesn't mean the groups were proven identical.

visual.fact: 'Similar' means no clear gap was seen

scenes.narration: There are other limits. Women weren't randomly assigned to a menopause stage, so the groups also differ in age and health. The figures count women who stayed on treatment, so results counting everyone who started would likely be somewhat lower. The trials were funded by the drugmaker. And much of this has so far been shared at medical meetings, so the full details deserve close review.

items: Groups differ in age and health
Counts women who stayed on treatment

scenes.narration: It also tells us nothing about hormone therapy. If that's on your mind, it's a separate conversation for you and your clinician.
So, the honest summary: in these trials, menopause stage didn't appear to hold back weight loss much. Encouraging, not final.
But weight loss is only half the story after menopause. The other half is where a lot of people slip, and we'll get to it right after side effects.
scenes.retention_device: New open loop (paid off in 'Muscle and bone')

scenes.narration: First, what taking it can feel like.
Like other GLP-1 medicines, orforglipron's most common side effects in the trials were digestive: nausea, constipation, diarrhea and vomiting.
Most were mild to moderate and tended to appear while the dose was being stepped up. Some people did stop treatment because of side effects, more often than on placebo.
What helps many people: smaller meals, eating slowly, stopping at the first sign of fullness, and going easy on greasy or very rich food.
Sip fluids through the day, especially if you're losing fluids from vomiting or diarrhea. Dehydration can make you feel worse, and in some cases it can strain the kidneys.
If side effects are hard to live with, tell your prescriber rather than pushing through or changing anything on your own. And severe or persistent belly pain is a reason to get checked promptly.
Now, the other half of the story.
Remember SWAN: lean mass starts slipping during the menopause transition. And when anyone loses weight, on a GLP-1 or not, part of what's lost is lean tissue, not just fat.

visual.stock_query: scale showing fat and muscle blocks

scenes.narration: Bone matters too. Estrogen helps protect bone, so bone loss speeds up after menopause, one reason osteoporosis is more common in older women.
That's why two habits sit at the center of GLP-1 lifestyle advice: strength training and enough protein.
The World Health Organization recommends muscle-strengthening activity on at least two days a week for adults, and adds balance and strength training for people sixty-five and older.
That doesn't have to mean a gym. Resistance bands, body-weight squats, wall push-ups or a pair of dumbbells at home can all count. Start light, and build gradually.

visual.stock_query: woman doing squats in living room

scenes.narration: Muscle-strengthening and weight-bearing exercise also load your bones, which is one reason they're recommended for bone health.

Then protein. On a GLP-1, appetite drops, so protein can quietly fall short. A joint advisory from four US obesity and nutrition societies recommends prioritizing protein while on these medicines, along with fiber-rich whole foods.

In practice: a protein source at every meal. Eggs or Greek yogurt at breakfast. Fish, chicken, tofu, lentils or beans later in the day. It can help to eat the protein first, while your appetite is strongest.
If you have kidney disease or another health condition, ask your care team what protein amount is right for you.
Put those habits next to the menopause data, and a clear plan comes into focus. Here it is.
Your takeaway checklist.
One: in these trials, menopause stage didn't appear to hold back weight loss much. Encouraging, but post-hoc.
Two: if you have type 2 diabetes, weight loss on a GLP-1 tends to be lower on average. That's expected, and blood sugar benefits count too.

items: Type 2 diabetes: less loss on average

scenes.narration: Three: strength train at least two days a week. Four: protein at every meal, plus fiber and fluids.
Five: report side effects to your prescriber, and never adjust your medicine on your own.
And most important: orforglipron is a prescription medicine. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it, or any GLP-1, is right for you.
Weight is just one measure of health. Strength, energy, blood sugar and blood pressure all count too.
Next up: how to keep your muscle on a GLP-1, with a simple five-part checklist. Subscribe to InforMed so it's waiting for you.

factcheck.summary:
Content check: PASS, with 3 minor wording and source fixes below.

I checked the core numbers against Lilly's press release, which is carried on PR Newswire and Lilly's investor site. They are all correct:
- **ATTAIN-1, highest dose, by menopause stage:** 12.8%, 14.4% and 14.1% weight loss.
- **ATTAIN-2, highest dose, by stage:** 11.3%, 8.9% and 13.6%.
- **Group sizes on the highest dose:** 171, 142 and 152 in ATTAIN-1; 10, 33 and 109 in ATTAIN-2.
- **Women losing at least 5% of body weight:** up to 82.7% on the drug vs about 30% on placebo.
- **ADA presentation:** June 2026.
- **Analysis type:** the Lilly poster page confirms it was a post-hoc analysis that counted women who stayed on treatment.

Other checks:
- **Pill details:** The FDA approval of Foundayo (1 April 2026) and the 12.4% average weight loss at the highest dose in ATTAIN-1 are confirmed.
- **Background studies:** The descriptions of SWAN, the 2008 visceral-fat study, STEP 1 (~15%) and STEP 2 (<10%), the WHO 2020 activity guidelines, the 2013 US obesity guideline (3–5% weight loss) and the four-society nutrition advisory match what the published papers say.
- **Framing:** It is careful. The script says the analysis is post-hoc, explains that ATTAIN-2 groups were small, notes the analysis counted women who stayed on treatment and that the trials were company-funded, and says "similar" doesn't mean "identical". It also says the reason results held steady is a plausible idea that wasn't tested.
- **Safety:** The script includes a caveat on protein for people with kidney disease and says not to change medicine on your own. It flags belly pain as a reason to get checked and includes the "talk to your prescriber" line. It gives no doses and names no gray-market sources.

**Fixes needed:**
1. **s02:** the EASD meeting runs 28 Sep–2 Oct 2026, so "presented again … in September" is premature.
2. **s19/s20:** these cite the ATTAIN-1 paper (S6) for claims about ATTAIN-2. They should cite the ATTAIN-2 paper in The Lancet.
3. **S1b title:** matches the Lilly page (no change needed).

**Sources I couldn't open directly:**
- The Pharmacy Times (S3) and HCPLive (S2) pages returned a 403 error. I confirmed their titles and URLs through search results.
- The Lilly investor page for the FDA approval (S1c) timed out. I confirmed it through search.
- PubMed (S12) showed a CAPTCHA. I confirmed the advisory's title and content through search.
